question: Bhagat Singh and ________ threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Batukeshwar Dutt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 to protest against the repressive Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill.
 
• The intent of the bombing was not to cause harm but to make the "deaf" British rulers hear India's demand for freedom.
 
• They shouted slogans like "Inquilab Zindabad" (Long live the revolution) and threw pamphlets outlining their cause.
 
• Both Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt voluntarily surrendered to the police after the bombing and were arrested on the spot.
 
• This event gained significant attention and brought the Indian independence movement to the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhagat Singh:** A revolutionary socialist, Bhagat Singh is considered one of the most influential freedom fighters in India's struggle for independence. He was known for his radical approach and sacrifice for the nation.
 
• **Batukeshwar Dutt:** A close associate of Bhagat Singh, Batukeshwar Dutt was a revolutionary freedom fighter who participated in many activities against British rule, including the Assembly bombing.
 
• **Central Legislative Assembly Bombing:** This act was a symbolic protest against British oppression and aimed to spark awareness among Indians about the need for independence.
 
• **Repressive Bills:** The Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill were introduced by the British to curb civil liberties and workers' rights in India, which led to widespread dissent among Indians.
 
• **Outcome:** Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt’s actions inspired the youth of India and became a rallying point for the independence movement. They were later tried and convicted for their roles in revolutionary activities.
